I can't even focus on LeetCode because every time I catch my reflection in the monitor, I just feel like this giant, lazy failure who doesn't deserve a good package anyway.

Everyone is posting pictures from the college fest on WhatsApp and Instagram, looking so effortless and thin. I spent the whole weekend locked in my hostel room because my face is ruined from stress acne and none of my clothes hide my stomach anymore. I'm literally failing my labs, and on top of that, I look like a complete mess compared to them—it's like my body is punishing me for not handling this semester well.

My relatives came over during the semester break and the first thing my aunt said wasn't about my CGPA, it was 'you've put on so much weight, look at your cousin who is preparing for UPSC and still stays so active'. I already feel like a failure for having two backlogs, and now my parents are looking at me with this sheer disappointment because I don't even look presentable. I feel so disgusting and invisible, like my physical existence is just an embarrassment to everyone around me.

We have our final year project evaluations next week and I'm terrified of standing in front of the whole department for the presentation. I know my coding part inside out, but all I can think about is how fat I look in formal pants and how everyone in the seminar hall will be judging my body instead of my slides. I'm seriously considering skipping the presentation and taking a zero because the thought of being stared at makes my chest so tight I can barely breathe.

Sitting in the hostel mess is pure torture lately. I see these thin guys from my branch eating plates of fried food while talking about their 15 LPA internships, and here I am, feeling guilty for even touching a chapati because I've gained 10 kgs since joining college. I'm starving myself during coding labs just to 'make up' for eating lunch, but then I end up bingeing late at night while debugging and the self-hatred is just eating me alive.

Everyone in my batch getting those 20 LPA packages looks so neat and put together, and then there's me. I've spent the last six months stress-eating Maggi during late-night DSA labs, and now my placement blazer won't even button up properly. I had to sit through a pre-placement talk today feeling so bloated and disgusting, convinced the recruiters were judging my double chin instead of my resume.

My WhatsApp group is flooded with photos from everyone's summer internships in Bangalore, and they all look so incredibly fit and aesthetic in their corporate casuals. Meanwhile, the hostel mess food and stress from backlogs have made me gain 12 kilos, and I honestly dread looking in the mirror or joining the group video calls. I feel like my body is a physical manifestation of my failure compared to them.

We have a group discussion round for a mock placement drive tomorrow, and my face has completely broken out from the stress of these midterms. I can't even focus on my talking points because I'm so terrified that everyone will just stare at my terrible skin and judge me. I just want to skip the viva entirely and hide in my hostel room because I feel so ugly next to my peers.

My dad called me today, and instead of asking how my end-semester exams went, his first comment was about how bloated and exhausted I look on the WhatsApp video call. He then immediately started comparing me to our neighbor's son who apparently lost weight, cracked an off-campus offer, and looks like a model. It made me feel so small, like I'm failing both academically and physically in their eyes.

I tried going to the campus gym to deal with my anxiety over failing my coding run, but everyone there is so muscular and confident. I looked at myself in the mirrors next to these guys who effortlessly bench-press plates, and I just felt incredibly weak, skinny, and pathetic. I ended up leaving after ten minutes and now I'm just sitting in my room, feeling too ashamed to even go to the mess for dinner.

I had to buy a blazer for the upcoming placement drives and literally none of the standard sizes fit me properly. I looked at myself in the trial room mirror and just wanted to throw up—I've put on so much weight from stress-eating during late-night DSA labs. Meanwhile, my roommate looks like a model in his slim-fit suit and already got shortlisted for the day-1 tech interview. How am I supposed to pitch myself to recruiters when I feel like an absolute blob who can't even manage his own body?

I failed my OS midterms and spent the last three days ordering junk food in my hostel room. I took a bath today and realized my stomach is bloating so badly, my old jeans won't even button up. I look at the other girls in my branch who somehow stay skinny and active while maintaining a 9+ CGPA, and I just feel disgusting and undisciplined. I’m failing my exams and failing my body, and I don't even want to step out of my room for mess food anymore.

Everyone in my wing is suddenly into lifting and hitting the campus gym, and I feel so small and pathetic next to them. I'm struggling with backlogs and barely have time to sleep, let alone cook high-protein meals, while these guys are posting progress pics on WhatsApp and getting compliments from everyone. I caught my reflection in the library glass doors today and I just looked so weak and hollowed out—like my academic failure is literally written all over my face and body.

I went home for Diwali after surviving a brutal semester of system design projects and placement prep. Instead of asking how I was, the first thing my mom said was, 'Why have you gotten so dark and bloated, look at your cousin who is also doing BTech but looks so fresh.' I literally went to my room and cried. I'm burning myself out to secure a good package, but to my family, my exhaustion is just an aesthetic failure compared to everyone else.

Our batch is organizing a graduation trip and they want to do a group photoshoot, but I'm planning to skip the whole thing because I hate how I look right now. I've gained almost 15 kgs since freshman year due to PCOS and thyroid issues worsened by exam stress, and looking at the old photos of me next to my friends makes me want to die. I don't want to ruin their perfect group pictures with my bloated face, so I'll probably just make up some excuse about working on my thesis.

I’ve been sitting at my desk for 14 hours a day prepping for placements, surviving on instant noodles and chai. I looked in the mirror today before my mock interview and I barely recognize myself—I've gained so much weight, my face is bloated, and my skin is ruined from the stress. My roommate goes to the gym, cracks his DSA sheets, and looks like a model, while I feel like an absolute slob who doesn't even deserve to be on a corporate panel.

We have our formal group discussions tomorrow for the tech consultancy drive, and I tried on my blazer. It doesn't even button up anymore because of the stress-eating during midterms, and I just broke down on my hostel floor. Everyone else looks so sharp and put-together in their LinkedIn headshots, and here I am, looking like a complete failure before I even open my mouth to speak.

My hair is thinning like crazy and my face is covered in cystic acne from pulled all-nighters for the OS and DBMS labs. In the metro today, I saw these guys from my batch looking so fresh, talking about their 12 LPA packages, and I just hid my face in my hoodie. I feel so ugly and worthless, like my physical deterioration is proof that I can't even handle basic engineering life.

Everyone is posting photos from the cultural fest, and I look so incredibly thin and skeletal next to my gym-going friends. My relatives keep making comments on video calls like 'Do they not feed you in the hostel?' and it makes me want to scream. I’m studying 10 hours a day to clear my backlogs, but all people see is a weak, sickly guy who can't even take care of himself.

I scrolled through my class WhatsApp group and saw everyone's photos from the graduation trip, looking incredibly fit and happy. I skipped the trip because I was stuck doing remedial coding labs, and now I’ve gained 15 kgs and feel completely invisible. I feel like I've failed on every front—my grades are average, my body is ruined, and I'm just watching everyone else live their best lives from my dark hostel room.

I spent the entire semester sitting in the library coding for DSA labs and eating whatever oily mess the mess committee served. Now placements are starting next week, and everyone is buying these sharp, slim-fit formal suits and looking so incredibly put together. I tried on my old formal shirt today and the buttons were literally straining across my stomach; I looked in the mirror and just started crying. My flatmate is a 9.5 CGPA guy who also runs 5ks every morning, and here I am, bloated, fat, with dark circles, looking like a total wreck. How am I supposed to walk into an interview panel looking like this when everyone else looks like a model?

We took a group photo after the last end-sem exam and someone posted it on the batch WhatsApp group today. I feel sick to my stomach just looking at it. Everyone else looks so lean, happy, and vibrant, and I just look like a massive, shapeless blob standing in the corner trying to hide behind someone else. I’ve gained 12 kgs since starting my prep for competitive exams, living on instant noodles and stress. I literally want to delete WhatsApp and never show my face in the lecture hall again; I feel so disgusting and inferior compared to them.

My mom called today and instead of asking how my mock tests went, she started talking about my cousin who just got placed at a FAANG company. Then she casually dropped, 'You should start eating less rice, you're gaining weight and it won't look good when we start looking for matches or when you go to office.' I felt this immediate wave of heat and nausea. I'm already dying trying to keep my CGPA above 8, and now even my physical body is a massive disappointment to my family compared to everyone else in our relative circle.

Everyone in my hostel wing is suddenly into 'bulking' and going to the campus gym, tracking macros, and showing off their progress. I tried going with them, but I felt so weak and small, like a child among men. My arms are like twigs and my chest is completely flat, while they all have these broad shoulders and talk about their protein intake. I can't even focus on my DSA labs anymore because every time I look in the mirror, I just feel this overwhelming sense of inadequacy and shame that I don't look like a 'real' guy.

I have my college fest coming up next week, and my friends wanted to go shopping for matching outfits. I went to the changing room with a size M shirt, and it wouldn't even go past my shoulders, let alone button up. I had to ask the sales assistant for an XL while my friends were all laughing and trying on slim-fit clothes outside. I felt like crying right there in the trial room. I ended up making an excuse about a pending assignment and ran back to my hostel room; I'm seriously thinking of skipping the fest entirely because I can't bear the thought of standing next to them in photos.

I had my first offline placement interview today. I spent hours prepping DSA and system design, but the moment I stood in front of the mirror in this cheap formal shirt I bought, I just wanted to melt into the floor. The buttons are straining, my face looks so bloated from all the late-night Maggi while coding, and everyone else in the placement cell lobby looked so sharp, fit, and effortless. I couldn't even make eye contact with the interviewer because I was so convinced they were judging how sloppy and out of shape I look, rather than my actual coding skills. I bombed the live coding round because my mind was just screaming about how huge I looked in that chair.

Everyone in my batch is posting their summer internship photos on LinkedIn and Instagram, and they all look so perfectly toned, tanned, and aesthetic in their corporate casuals. Meanwhile, my CGPA dropped to 6.8, I've gained 12 kilos from stress-eating during end-sems, and I look like a thumb. I literally skipped the class group photo today because I couldn't bear the thought of my double chin being preserved forever in the department archives next to all these gym-goers. I feel like an academic failure and a physical eyesore, like I'm failing at college in every possible dimension.

My parents came down for the convocation prep and the first thing my dad said wasn't congrats on the TCS offer, it was 'You've really let yourself go, look at your cousin Rohan, he's so lean and cracked the 20LPA package'. I spent the whole night in my hostel bathroom crying and pinching my waist. I feel so disgusting. I worked 14-hour days to get this backlog cleared and get placed, but all they see is my stomach hanging over my jeans, and now I don't even want to walk across the stage to get my degree.

I can't even go to the mess anymore. Every time I walk in, I feel like everyone is watching me load my plate, comparing how much I eat with how fat I am. There's this group of girls from the design department who always look like runway models, effortlessly skinny, and I'm just this blocky CS student who lives in oversized hoodies to hide my love handles. I ended up skipping lunch today and just survived on black coffee to avoid the stares. My brain is so foggy I can't even focus on my compiler design lab, but the fear of being seen and judged is paralyzing.

I got selected for the college cultural fest dance team, but during the first costume trial today, they didn't have my size for the performance outfits. The coordinator had to yell across the room to ask someone to fetch a 'plus-sized' set from the storage room while all the juniors watched. I felt so exposed and humiliated, especially when I saw my reflection next to the lead dancers who are literally half my size. Now I'm sitting in the library stairwell, looking at my labs that are due at midnight, and I just want to pack my bags, drop out of this engineering college, and disappear so no one ever has to look at me again.
